{{short description|Dutch physicist}}
'''Frank Willem Jan Hekking''' (28 September 1964 – 15 May 2017) was a Dutch physicist working at [[Grenoble Alpes University|Université Grenoble Alpes]] in [[Grenoble]], France. He is notable for his contributions in theory of [[mesoscopic physics|mesoscopic]] [[superconductivity]], in particular, [[Andreev reflection]] and [[Josephson effect]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://frank-memorial.sciencesconf.org|title=Frank Hekking Memorial Workshop|year=2018|publisher=[[École de physique des Houches]]|accessdate=31 January 2018}}</ref> He was a member of [[Institut Universitaire de France]] since 2012 until his death.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iufrance.fr/detail-de-lactualite/101.html|title=Deces du professeur Frank Hekking|year=2017|publisher=[[Institut Universitaire de France]]|language=French|accessdate=31 January 2018}}</ref>

In 1992, Hekking received a PhD degree from [[Delft University of Technology]], where he worked under supervision of {{illm|Gerd Schön|de|}}. After postdoctoral appointments at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology|University of Karlsruhe]], the [[University of Minnesota]], the [[University of Cambridge]], and [[Ruhr University Bochum]], he became a professor at Université Grenoble Alpes. He was attached to Laboratoire de Physique et de Modélisation des Milieux Condensés of [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]], and he was a director of this laboratory on two occasions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sfpnet.fr/deces-de-frank-hekking|title=Décès de Frank Hekking|date=May 2017|publisher=[[Société Française de Physique]]|language=French|accessdate=31 January 2018}}</ref>
